topics.title: Meet the 5-String Banjo
topics.short: The parts of a 5-string banjo, open-back and resonator banjos, how the strings are numbered, and the short 5th string that gives the banjo its sound.

topics.title: Where the Banjo Comes From
topics.short: A short, plain history of the banjo: its West African roots, the instruments made by enslaved Africans in the Americas, the minstrel stage, old-time string bands and bluegrass.

topics.title: Holding the Banjo
topics.short: How to sit with a banjo, use a strap, place the fretting hand, and set up the picking hand for three-finger style (with picks) and for clawhammer (without).

topics.title: Tuning to Open G
topics.short: Open G tuning (g D G B D), tuning with the microphone tuner or by ear, the 5th-fret method that checks each string against the next, and tips that keep a banjo in tune.

topics.title: Reading Banjo Tab
topics.short: How banjo tablature works: five lines for five strings, fret numbers, the 5th string’s numbers, rhythm under the tab, the picking letters T I M and S D T, and the marks for hammer-ons, pull-offs and slides.

topics.title: Your First Chords: G, C, D7 and D
topics.short: Reading a banjo chord diagram, the open G chord, and the C, D7 and D shapes that go with it, with an exercise for changing between them.

topics.title: Three-Finger Picking: Thumb, Index, Middle
topics.short: The picking hand for bluegrass banjo: thumb pick and finger picks, which finger plays which string, anchoring, single notes and pinches, slowly and evenly.

topics.title: The Forward Roll
topics.short: The most important pattern in bluegrass banjo: thumb, index, middle over and over, eight notes to a bar, on G, C and D7.

topics.title: Backward, Alternating-Thumb and Forward-Reverse Rolls
topics.short: Three more rolls every bluegrass banjo player uses: the backward roll, the alternating-thumb roll and the forward-reverse roll, with a practice piece that mixes them.

topics.title: Melody Inside the Roll
topics.short: How Scruggs-style banjo carries a tune: the melody notes sit inside the rolls, and the other notes ring around them. Your first full tune with rolls, Boil Them Cabbage Down.

topics.title: Clawhammer: The Bum-Ditty
topics.short: The old-time downstroke style: hand shape, the strike with the back of the fingernail, the brush, the thumb on the 5th string, and the bum-ditty rhythm on G, C and D7.

topics.title: Clawhammer Melody: Your First Tune
topics.short: Aiming the clawhammer strike at the melody note, letting the brush carry the next beat, and Boil Them Cabbage Down in clawhammer from start to finish.

topics.title: Hammer-Ons, Pull-Offs and Slides
topics.short: Notes made by the fretting hand alone: the hammer-on, the pull-off and the slide, how they are written in tab, and how they sound in three-finger and clawhammer playing.

topics.title: Licks, Fill-Ins and Endings
topics.short: Short ready-made phrases for three-finger banjo: the slide lick, hammer-on and pull-off licks, a low-string lick, fill-ins for long melody notes and a lick to end a tune.

topics.title: Hymns and Slow Tunes
topics.short: Putting rolls, chords and melody together in slow Southern hymn tunes: How Firm a Foundation with the melody on the thumb, and Amazing Grace in 3/4 time.

topics.title: Drop-Thumb and Double Thumbing
topics.short: Intermediate clawhammer: double thumbing (the thumb after every strike) and drop-thumb (the thumb dropping onto the inside strings to play melody notes between the beats).

topics.title: Double C and Open D Tunings
topics.short: Why banjo players retune: double C (g C G C D) for tunes in C and D, open D (f♯ D F♯ A D) for tunes in D, how to get there from open G, and the main chords in each.

topics.title: The Capo and the 5th String
topics.short: Playing in other keys with a capo: which fret for which key, what to do with the short 5th string (retuning, spikes, a 5th-string capo), and how tab and chord names are counted from the capo.

topics.title: More Chords and Moveable Shapes
topics.short: Em, Am, A, E7, F and Bm in open G tuning, then the three moveable chord shapes (barre, F shape and D shape) that let you play any major chord anywhere on the neck.

topics.title: Scales and the Fretboard
topics.short: The G major scale in first position on the banjo, the notes on each string, the G major pentatonic scale that so many Southern tunes use, and the D major scale for fiddle tunes in D.

topics.title: Up the Neck
topics.short: Leaving first position: the D shape at the 7th fret, finding melody notes higher on the neck, and playing the B part of Fisher’s Hornpipe there.

topics.title: Fiddle Tunes on the Banjo
topics.short: How old-time and bluegrass fiddle tunes are built (A and B parts, each played twice), the keys fiddlers use and which banjo tuning or capo fits each, and how to learn a tune by ear.

topics.title: Backup, Jamming and Practice
topics.short: Playing behind a singer or another instrument: bluegrass vamping with closed chords, rolls as backup, clawhammer backup, how a jam works, and a simple practice plan.
